rationale:
Evidence from iteration 1 (R2A, 60 trials): every run still ended off track on all three tracks, and the score fell from 56.08 to 54.27. Widening the sensors removed line loss on the oval (0 events) but did not keep the robot on the line. Max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 m, just above the 0.06 m limit, on every track, and progress was only 0.11 to 0.15. Oscillation on the oval fell to 0.072, but on the s-bend and slalom it stayed near 0.14. So the failure is not sensor loss. The robot drifts about 6 cm from the line through the bends, probably from overshoot at kp 4.0 (a full-scale signal gives about 1400 PWM of differential) and the fixed motor mismatch, which the integral term must cancel.

Changes: (1) kp 4.0 to 3.5, to reduce overshoot and the oscillation that pushes the error past 0.06 m. (2) ki 0.05 back to 0.1. Iteration 0 had ki 0.1 and similar max_error, and the integral is needed to cancel the constant left/right mismatch, so lowering it did not help. (3) base_speed 1.4 to 1.2. Survival comes before speed: a run that stays on track and reaches progress 1 is worth far more than an early exit, and the 3 s finish needs about 1.5 m/s, which I will raise to once the robot survives. (4) Sensor footprint 0.012 to 0.016, so each sensor sees more tape at the 6 cm offsets and the signal is smoother. Geometry positions and weights stay as in iteration 1, so the steering sign is unchanged. kd stays at 0.3 to damp the jitter.

Expected result: max_error below 0.06 on the oval and s-bend, line_loss_events near 0, and completion on at least the oval. Finish time will be well over 3 s at this speed. Risks: lower kp may leave the robot slow to correct on the sharpest slalom bends, and the larger footprint may blur the edges of the tape. Hypotheses to check next: (a) kp is the main driver of the 0.06 m overshoot; (b) survival at base_speed 1.2 is enough to get completion=1 or progress near 1. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation, per track and per seed.
